title: A boatman’s tip
body:
A boatman who ferries porters to the anchorage waits by the steps of your house. For a few coins, he says, he will tell you which ship tomorrow carries more than she declares. He has rowed out to her twice tonight, and each time a man aboard paid him to forget it.

He will not say who else has paid him today.

choices.label: Pay for the name
choices.outcome_text: He names a ship due on the morning tide and takes your coins. It may be the truth. It may be a rival’s way to keep your inspectors busy while another ship slips through.

choices.label: Send him away
choices.outcome_text: You do not buy rumours at your own door. The boatman shrugs and rows off toward the Upeh landing, where someone else may pay.
